# Objective

In Lab 5, you made cleaning decisions explicit and reproducible in a data-processing pipeline. In this lab, you will inspect a website's scraping guidance, complete a small HTML-extraction function, collect a dataset, and preserve the extracted records before cleaning.

You will work with the official [October 2025 General Conference index](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2025/10?lang=eng). The goal is to collect metadata and article text for one conference.

## Before you begin

- Work only within the designated October 2025 conference.
- Complete the source-guidance check below before making automated requests.
- Collect your raw dataset from the live website. Do not substitute a prebuilt dataset or someone else's saved HTML. The small HTML examples below are only for practicing title extraction.
- Keep requests polite and bounded. The supplied script limits the number of pages and waits between requests.
- Once collection works, keep the raw CSV unchanged. Render this document from the saved data rather than scraping again on every render.
- If access is prohibited or collection fails, document the issue and contact the instructor. Do not bypass restrictions or expand the scrape to find a workaround.

# Part 2: Complete and run the scraper

## 3. Write a title-extraction function

Read `scripts/scrape_data.py`. Most of the scraper is supplied. Your coding task is to complete `extract_title(soup)`.

The function receives a Beautiful Soup object and should return a string:

1. Use `soup.select_one("h1")` to find the first primary heading.
2. If the heading exists and its text is not blank, return its text.
3. Otherwise, return the text of the `<title>` element if it exists.
4. If neither element provides a title, return an empty string.

Use `node.get_text(" ", strip=False)` to extract text from an element. You may use `.strip()` to check whether text is blank, but return the original extracted string. Standardizing whitespace belongs in the cleaning step.

Replace the `raise NotImplementedError(...)` line with your code. You do not need to change the request-handling or link-discovery functions.

Try your function on these small examples before making requests:

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from scripts.scrape_data import extract_title

heading_example = BeautifulSoup(
    "<html><head><title>Browser title</title></head>"
    "<body><h1>Practice talk title</h1></body></html>",
    "html.parser",
)
fallback_example = BeautifulSoup(
    "<html><head><title>Fallback title</title></head><body></body></html>",
    "html.parser",
)

print(extract_title(heading_example))
print(extract_title(fallback_example))
```

The results should be `Practice talk title` and `Fallback title`.

# Part 4: Clean after collection

## 7. Create a processed dataset

Keep `data/raw/talks_raw.csv` unchanged. Create a separate processed file at `data/processed/talks_clean.csv`. Use the cleaning principles from Lab 5: make transformations explicit, preserve meaningful missing values, and validate the result.

At minimum:

- remove any session overview or index pages if they were collected;
- standardize leading/trailing whitespace in title and speaker fields;
- create a `year` column from the conference label;
- calculate `num_words` from the extracted `text`; and
- retain the source URL as `link`.

For this lab, define `num_words` as the number of whitespace-separated tokens in the entire extracted article text. It is an article-text word count, not an exact count of spoken words. Leave the count missing when the source text is missing.

Do not overwrite raw text. If you create a normalized text field in the processed data, document the transformation and retain the original text in the raw CSV.

# Part 5: Responsible and reproducible collection

## 8. Reliability and ethics

A scraper can collect publicly visible data and still be unreliable or inappropriate. Consider request load, site terms, attribution, copyright, personal information, and whether the data are necessary for the task.
